body.statement:
Fix \(m,\lambda,\alpha\), a probability vector \(\pi\) on \(\mathcal O_N\), and numbers \(\eta_n\ge0\).  Define
\[
 \beta=(1-\alpha)\sum_n\eta_n,
 \qquad
 k_h=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T_N}\left[
 \sum_{n:\tau(n)=t}\eta_n\rho_{n,m,h}(\lambda)
 -\sum_n\pi_n\rho_{n,m,h}(\lambda)
 \right]_+,
\]
and \(F(a)=\sum_hk_ha^h\).  If \(v^1,\ldots,v^q\) are all vertices of \(\mathcal A_\lambda\), and \(\mathsf T_F\) is the symmetric \(N\)-linear form whose diagonal is \(F\), then every legal common channel satisfies
\[
 V_m(Q_a)\ge\beta-F(a)
 \ge\beta-\max_{j_1,\ldots,j_N}\mathsf T_F(v^{j_1},\ldots,v^{j_N}).
\]
body.proof_tex:
For every probability vector \(\pi\) and every \(\eta\ge0\), set each upper-bound dual slack equal to the positive part of the coverage-weighted density minus the loss-prior density.  This makes every dual inequality obtained from the fixed-confidence program feasible.  Substituting
\[
 P_{n,m,Q_a}(h)=\rho_{n,m,h}(\lambda)a^h.
\]
Because \(a^h\ge0\), it passes through the positive part: \([a^hx]_+=a^h[x]_+\).  Weak duality then gives
\[
 V_m(Q_a)\ge (1-\alpha)\sum_n\eta_n-\sum_hk_ha^h
 =\beta-F(a).
\]

For a histogram \(h\), let \(M_h=N!/\prod_Sh_S!\).  Define the ordered tensor entry corresponding to \((S_1,\ldots,S_N)\) to be \(k_h/M_h\), where \(h\) records the multiplicities of the \(S_i\)'s.  There are \(M_h\) ordered tuples with that histogram, so \(\mathsf T_F(a,\ldots,a)=F(a)\).  Compactness of \(\mathcal A_\lambda\) and the finite-dimensional polytope representation give \(a=\sum_j\theta_jv^j\), with \(\theta_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_j\theta_j=1\).  Multilinearity yields
\[
 F(a)=\sum_{j_1,\ldots,j_N}
 \theta_{j_1}\cdots\theta_{j_N}
 \mathsf T_F(v^{j_1},\ldots,v^{j_N}).
\]
The coefficients in this sum are nonnegative and sum to one.  Hence \(F(a)\) is no larger than the maximum displayed tensor entry, proving the second inequality.
